body.heading: The inner commentator
paragraphs: Most of us have an inner voice that would be fired from any coaching job: it generalises (“I always mess up”), it predicts (“everyone will think I'm stupid”), and it never mentions the nine things that went fine.
That voice feels like honesty, but it is usually just habit — an old recording. Noticing it is the first step: you cannot argue with a commentary you have not realised is playing.

body.heading: Borrow a friend's voice
paragraphs: A practical trick: ask what you would say to a friend in the same situation. Almost nobody tells a friend “you're hopeless” over a failed test or an awkward message. We offer perspective, proportion and a next step.
Write that friend-version down if you need to, and read it back. It may feel artificial at first — most new habits do. Artificial and kinder beats automatic and cruel.

takeaway: Talk to yourself the way you'd talk to a friend — it is a learnable habit.
